title: Primitive specialization of a generic line section over a trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$ and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nonempty geometrically connected fibres, meaning that every residue-field fibre remains nonempty and connected after extension to an algebraic closure. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Put $X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $X_k=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $C$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], with restrictions $C_K,C_k$ defined by tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. For every nonzero global section $s_K\in\Gamma(X_K,C_K)$, there exist an integer $m\in\mathbf Z$ and a global section $s\in\Gamma(X,C)$ such that $s|_{X_K}=\pi^m s_K$ and $s|_{X_k}$ is nonzero. No properness or completeness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1, part (2), applied to local coefficients of a rational line section after subtracting its valuation along the unique special-fibre divisor; descent.tex Tag 036D, lemma-regular-local-smooth, supplies regularity over a DVR. Agent-extracted geometric section lemma, not a verbatim Stacks statement.

proof.text: The DVR $R$ is Noetherian since every ideal is principal. Every nonzero denominator in $R$ is a unit times a nonnegative power of $\pi$, so $K=R[1/\pi]$. The principal-localization open immersion and its base change identify $X_K\to X$ with the open $D_X(\pi)$; on an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ it is $U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}K=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RK)=\operatorname{Spec}A[1/\pi]\subset U$ by the affine fibre-product lemma. Pullback of modules along this open immersion is restriction, so $C_K=C|_{D_X(\pi)}$ and $\Gamma(V_K,C_K)=\Gamma(D_V(\pi),C)$ for every open $V\subset X$. The finite-presentation hypothesis includes quasi-compactness, so $X$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final assertion; schemes.tex Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine); morphisms.tex Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation).

proof.text: The projection $X_{\overline K}\to X_K$ is surjective: over an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}D\subset X_K$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(D\otimes_K\overline K)\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ by the affine fibre-product lemma, and this is field-extension faithful flatness followed by surjectivity on prime spectra. A decomposition of $X_K$ into two nonempty disjoint clopen subsets would pull back to such a decomposition of $X_{\overline K}$, contradicting the fibre hypothesis. Thus $X_K$ is nonempty and connected. Smoothness is preserved by base change, so $X_K$ is regular by smooth-over-a-field regularity. The connected regular scheme lemma now makes $X_K$ integral.

source.place: Tag 056S (lemma-smooth-regular); properties.tex Tags 0569 (lemma-regular-normal), 033N (lemma-normal-locally-Noetherian); algebra.tex faithful flatness under field extension.

proof.text: For a nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, restriction of smoothness and the affine smoothness equivalence make $R\to A$ a smooth ring map, hence flat and finitely presented. Flat torsion-freeness gives injectivity of multiplication by $\pi$ on $A$, and hence $A\hookrightarrow A[1/\pi]$: a fraction-kernel element is killed by a power of $\pi$. Since $A\ne0$, its localization is nonzero. This localization is the coordinate ring of the nonempty affine open $U_K\subset X_K$, so it is a domain by Step 2. Its subring $A$ is a domain too. This proves $X$ integral. Also $A$ is Noetherian by the finite-type algebra theorem over the Noetherian ring $R$. Thus $X$ is locally Noetherian. In particular, on $X$ and on $X_K$, sections of an invertible module over any nonempty open inject into its generic stalk.

source.place: Tags 00TA (lemma-smooth-syntomic), 00SL (definition-lci), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); more-algebra.tex Tag 0539 (lemma-valuation-ring-torsion-free-flat), flat implies torsion free; properties.tex Tag 01OK (definition-integral).

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $U_1,\ldots,U_r$ trivializing $C$, using quasi-compactness from Step 1 and local freeness of rank one. On $U_i$, apply affine basic-open localization of quasi-coherent sections to $s_K|_{(U_i)_K}$ and the coefficient $\pi$, obtaining $N_i\ge0$ and $t_i$ with $t_i|_{(U_i)_K}=\pi^{N_i}s_K$. Set $N=\max_iN_i$ and replace $t_i$ by $\pi^{N-N_i}t_i$. These sections agree on every overlap: their restrictions to its generic open agree, hence their germs at the common generic point agree, and injectivity into the generic stalk from Step 3 forces equality (empty overlaps need no check). The sheaf axiom glues them to $t\in\Gamma(X,C)$ with $t|_{X_K}=\pi^Ns_K\ne0$.

source.place: Tags 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine), 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves); explicit affine denominator lemma read at lean/WeilConjectures/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Tilde.lean:112-144; finite-cover gluing is the sheaf axiom.

proof.text: Choose $x\in X_k$, which exists by the nonempty-fibre hypothesis. Put $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. An affine chart from Step 3 has Noetherian coordinate ring, and $B$ is its prime localization; hence $B$ is Noetherian. The module $C_x$ is free of rank one, so finite. The element $\pi$ belongs to the maximal ideal of $B$, because its image in $\kappa(x)$ factors through $k=R/(\pi)$ and is zero. The germ $t_x$ is nonzero: its image in $C_\eta$ is the nonzero generic germ of $\pi^Ns_K$, by the injectivity for $C_K$ and $C$ in the generic-stalk lemma. Apply Krull intersection with the ideal $I=\pi B$ and the finite module $C_x$ to obtain $\bigcap_{j\ge0}\pi^jC_x=0$. Consequently there is $b\ge0$ with $t_x\notin\pi^bC_x$.

source.place: Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module), part (2), equivalently local form Tag 00IP (lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero); Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: Let $T=\{j\in\mathbf N:\ t=\pi^jv\text{ for some }v\in\Gamma(X,C)\}$. It contains $0$. Every $j\in T$ has $t_x\in\pi^jC_x$, so Step 5 bounds $j<b$. The finite nonempty subset $T$ of the natural numbers therefore has a largest element $a$. Choose $s\in\Gamma(X,C)$ with $t=\pi^as$. Restricting to $X_K$, where $\pi$ is invertible, gives $s|_{X_K}=\pi^{N-a}s_K$.

source.place: Elementary maximal-divisibility consequence of Tag 00IQ; finite subsets of the natural numbers and cancellation by the invertible scalar on the generic fibre.

proof.text: Suppose $s|_{X_k}=0$. On a trivializing affine $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, write $s=c_ie_i$, where $e_i$ is the chosen basis of $C$. By the affine fibre-product lemma $U_i\cap X_k=U_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}k=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i/\pi A_i)$, with projection $a\mapsto a\bmod\pi$, and $C_k$ restricted there is the tensor inverse image of $C|_{U_i}$ (open-immersion pullback is restriction, and pullbacks compose). Tensor inverse image to $U_i\cap X_k$ sends this basis to a basis and the coefficient to $c_i\bmod\pi$. Vanishing therefore says $c_i=\pi d_i$ for some $d_i\in A_i$. Put $v_i=d_ie_i$. On overlaps $\pi(v_i-v_j)=0$, and multiplication by $\pi$ is injective locally by Step 3 and local freeness, so $v_i=v_j$. These sections glue to $v$ with $s=\pi v$. Then $t=\pi^{a+1}v$, contradicting maximality of $a$. Hence $s|_{X_k}\ne0$. With the integer $m=N-a$ this is precisely the required section.

source.place: Tag 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine); coefficient computation of tensor inverse image on the closed fibre, followed by the sheaf axiom. No surjectivity of global sections onto the special fibre is assumed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q22-c07fdf716 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the unsplit Q44 node, so the target is not weakened. The statement is true: X is integral and normal and X_k is the prime divisor (π). It has no new nodes, no repair note and no SGA source. I checked each of the 7 steps against the statements of the cited nodes. (1) K=R_π and X_K=D_X(π), and finite presentation gives quasi-compactness. (2) X_{K̄}→X_K is surjective by faithful flatness, so X_K is connected; smooth base change and smooth-over-field-regular make it regular; lem-sc-regular-connected-integral makes it integral. (3) R→A is smooth, hence flat; lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain makes π injective; A embeds in the domain A_π, so X is integral; A is Noetherian. (4) Basic-open denominator clearing works on a finite trivializing affine cover, and the local extensions glue by injectivity into the generic stalk. (5) Krull's intersection theorem (00IQ(2)) applies with I=πB ⊂ m_x on the free rank-1 stalk C_x, and t_x≠0. (6) The divisibility set is bounded, so it has a maximum a. (7) If s vanished on X_k, the local quotients by π would glue and contradict the maximality of a. Small cases tested: Spec R with negative m; A^1_R with s_K=π^{-d}(π+x); and Spec R ⊔ Spec K, which shows why the connectedness hypothesis is needed. Batch-5 finding: lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain is a Mathlib leaf (Module.Flat.torsion_eq_bot) of general commutative algebra with empty closure. It is neither part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality nor a step of their proofs, so I accept it. I also accept the six generic tool_uses (smooth clause of proper-base-change, smooth-over-field-regular, regular-connected-integral, smooth-ring-map-iff-affine, invertible-module-generic-stalk, affine basic-open localization). FIX (C1, two missing citations): steps 1, 2 and 7 identify U×_R K, X_K charts and U_i∩X_k with Spec of tensor products, and steps 4 and 7 use C_K=C|_{D(π)}, but neither fact was cited. I added lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra and lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction (both Mathlib leaves) to the step uses and proof_deps, with the identifications written out.
